what: Globus Medical makes spine implants: the screws, rods, cages and plates used to fuse and stabilise the spine, and the robotic systems and navigation that guide the surgery.
customers: Spine surgeons and hospitals, with implants sold case by case.
money: spine implants, trauma and joint products
moat: Surgeons trained on its implant system and robot, where the robot anchors the hospital to the whole implant range that works with it.
risks: Spine implant prices fall steadily under hospital purchasing pressure
The NuVasive merger has to be integrated without losing surgeons, who are loyal to representatives rather than companies
Surgeon and sales representative departures after a merger are a real risk
opportunities: 17 times earnings with an 18.3% net margin and $767M of free cash flow
Revenue grew from $958M to $2.9B in four years, mostly through the NuVasive merger
$557M of cash against $119M of debt, and analysts see about 36% upside
watch: Organic revenue growth excluding the merger, and robot placements.
